themes.theme: Long-term holding of stable market leaders
Buying early-life companies with high certainty

positions.commentary: Microsoft will always have a market position and is a stable company suitable for long-term holding without needing constant attention.
Amazon is an example of a company at the beginning of its life that you can buy, be sure of, and hold while sleuthing it year in and year out.
Intuit is an example of a company at the beginning of its life that you can buy, be sure of, and hold while sleuthing it year in and year out.

thesis: The episode argues that investors should focus on stable companies with enduring market positions, such as Microsoft, and early-life companies with high certainty, like Amazon and Intuit, which are suitable for long-term holding while conducting ongoing research.

claims.claim: Microsoft will always have a market position and is a stable company suitable for long-term holding without needing constant attention.
claims.quote: So be careful not to own stocks that need a lot of attention all the time. So again, to answer your question, Eddie, the execution, as far as the buying and the selling, it's not very onerous. In trading it is, but I don't do trading. And the research side, you have to like doing the sleuthing. You have to like to interact with people.

claims.claim: Amazon is an example of a company at the beginning of its life that you can buy, be sure of, and hold while sleuthing it year in and year out.
claims.quote: If you got a Microsoft or an Amazon or an Intuit or other companies at the beginning of their life, the way to make money is you buy them and you are absolutely sure of them and you keep sleuthing them year in, year out as you hold them and then you do nothing.

claims.claim: Intuit is an example of a company at the beginning of its life that you can buy, be sure of, and hold while sleuthing it year in and year out.
claims.quote: If you got a Microsoft or an Amazon or an Intuit or other companies at the beginning of their life, the way to make money is you buy them and you are absolutely sure of them and you keep sleuthing them year in, year out as you hold them and then you do nothing.

numbers.quote: So despite all the work going into the sleuthing part of analysis, you're right that you think that the picking stocks is only 30 to 40 percent of the investing art.

numbers.quote: The execution part is, I would say, 5% doing and 95% not doing.

numbers.quote: The new companies that you put in your portfolio shouldn't be very many of them.
